articles.title: Trump rips Zelensky amid Russia diesel deal feud: ‘I suggest they get a new leader’
articles.summary: President Trump on Saturday pushed back on criticism from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky to the White House’s decision to lift sanctions on Russian diesel amid the Russia-Ukraine war. The president told reporters outside the White House that Zelensky “could have settled this war many times,” but “chose not to.” “He wants to make problems for…
articles.body:
President Trump on Saturday pushed back on criticism from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky to the White House’s decision to lift sanctions on Russian diesel amid the Russia-Ukraine war.

The president told reporters outside the White House that Zelensky “could have settled this war many times,” but “chose not to.”

“He wants to make problems for the world,” Trump said. “He wants to make problems for our farmers, our ranchers with diesel fuel because Russia supplies a large portion of the diesel fuel throughout the world.”

The president said his administration told the Ukrainian leader not to “hit the diesel fuel,” but Zelensky ignored his request, referring to Ukraine’s decision to target Russian oil refineries in response to Moscow’s strikes on civilian infrastructure.

When pressed by a journalist about concerns this agreement could place Ukrainians at greater risk for Russian attacks, Trump responded, “I suggest they get a new leader who can make a deal.”

The deal, which was announced Friday, permits Russia to supply 300,000 tons of diesel to the U.S. and the global marketplace.

It comes as the president faces growing pressure to address concerns over mounting energy costs due to global fuel shortages during the U.S.’s military operations against Iran and the Russia-Ukraine war.

On Saturday, Zelensky warned the deal signaled to Russia that “it could simply keep attacking” Ukraine.

“Every additional billion dollars they can earn from exports will be spent on nothing but sourcing and importing critical components and equipment to manufacture weapons, upgrading ‘shaheds,’ producing missiles, and recruiting even more mercenaries to fight at the front,” the Ukrainian leader wrote in a post on the social platform X.

“Russia’s choice is war,” he continued. “And they will be ready to end it only when they feel that their ability to drag the war out is diminishing.”

Democratic lawmakers also denounced the move, with Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.) accusing the president of striking “a deal with the devil” to try to save his “flailing political fortunes.”

“This filthy deal will only aid and abet the same Putin who is helping the Iranians to target and try to kill American troops in the Middle East and who illegally and viciously invaded our ally Ukraine,” Schumer wrote on the social platform X .

Additionally, Pennsylvania Rep. Madeleine Dean (D) cast the move as a “desperate” attempt from President Trump to “escape the consequences of his failed Iran war.”

“Trump is preparing to stab Ukraine in the back and buy diesel from Putin,” Dean continued. “He’s helping fund Russia’s war machine, while our allies pay the price.”

articles.title: Photos: Thousands march across Europe to demand end to Israel’s war on Gaza
articles.summary: Demonstrations in London, Berlin, and Rome denounce ongoing Israeli attacks on Gaza ‘ceasefire’ anniversary.
articles.body:
Several thousand pro-Palestinian protesters have marched through European capitals, demanding an end to Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza.

In London, demonstrators moved past the British parliament carrying placards reading “End the genocide” and “Free Palestine”.

“We are here today to mark three years of the ongoing genocide in Gaza,” Aimee Shalan, director of the Palestine Solidarity Campaign, told the AFP news agency, calling for “full sanctions on Israel”.

A so-called ceasefire took effect a year ago, but Israel continues to strike Gaza on a near-daily basis. The attacks have killed some 1,450 Palestinians since the truce began, according to Gaza’s Health Ministry.

London’s Metropolitan Police said they made “several arrests”, including a man and a woman holding placards supporting Palestine Action, a group banned under UK law.

Officers had also warned they would use public order powers to compel anyone wearing face coverings to remove them, pledging “zero tolerance” for hate crimes.

In Berlin, about 3,500 people joined a march organised by United for Palestine, police said, setting off from a square between the chancellery and parliament. Many condemned Germany’s arms exports and longstanding military support for Israel.

Similar marches were held in Warsaw and Rome, where protesters denounced ongoing Israeli bombardment and their governments’ ties with Israel, echoing calls for an immediate and lasting ceasefire.

Israel’s genocide has left most of Gaza in ruins and killed more than 74,200 Palestinians since October 2023.

articles.summary: Haryana LoP Bhupinder Hooda alleges 70% paddy procurement pending, seeks MSP white paper; cites mandi congestion, delays, and distress sales below MSP.
articles.body: Chandigarh: Leader of opposition Bhupinder Singh Hooda on Saturday criticised the BJP govt in Haryana, alleging that 70% of the paddy across state mandis was yet to be procured.Addressing media persons alongside Thanesar MLA Ashok Arora at his residence, Hooda demanded a white paper on the state’s claim of providing MSP on 24 crops.Hooda said that of the 12 lakh metric tonnes of paddy that had arrived in mandis, the govt had procured only 30%. “Out of the procured stock, merely 17% has been lifted, leaving mandis completely choked with no storage space,” Hooda stated, citing administrative hurdles like portal delays, gate passes, capping, and verification backlogs affecting lakhs of acres.The former CM alleged that due to the lack of timely state intervention, distressed farmers were forced to sell paddy at rates Rs 400 below the MSP, while pearl millet (bajra) is trading Rs 800–Rs 900 lower per quintal than its fixed rate of Rs 2,900.“The CM promised Rs 3,100 per quintal during elections, but farmers are struggling to even get the standard MSP of Rs 2,441,” he added, citing severe losses in moong and bajra.
